actors.name: Beacon maintainer
actors.rationale: primary owner of public skill contract evolution

actors.name: Beacon operator
actors.rationale: consumes route, explainability, and challenge semantics

actors.name: workflow governance owner
actors.rationale: owns freeze, enforcement, and cross-surface consistency

capability_differences.name: support surface vs truth surface authority
capability_differences.rationale: v1.4.6 depends on explicit authority boundaries

state_machine.name: draft -> clarified -> frozen -> implemented -> verified
state_machine.rationale: anti-drift contracts must bind into the existing Beacon lifecycle rather than creating a new stage

happy_paths.name: public skill contract is tightened and machine-checkable before implementation

negative_paths.name: support surface overreaches into truth or gate authority
negative_paths.rationale: must be blocked by contract and lint checks

boundary_conditions.name: no new lifecycle stage and no external runtime dependency

exceptions.name: challenge verdict produced without route/evidence/state/gate binding
exceptions.rationale: must fail closed as free-form commentary

recovery_paths.name: clarify -> update contract surface -> re-freeze -> run anti-drift checks
recovery_paths.rationale: formal recovery path when contract drift is detected

risks.name: public skill docs stay descriptive instead of executable
risks.rationale: core risk v1.4.6 is meant to close

prd: Beacon v1.4.6 should freeze a stronger anti-drift skill contract layer.
The goal is not to copy external skill packs or reduce Beacon into a prompt library.
user_story: I want Beacon's public skills and support surfaces to carry stronger anti-drift contracts connected to evidence, state, and gate semantics,
So that host-visible behavior becomes harder to misuse before machine governance must intervene.
qa: high-risk challenge outputs bind back to evidence, state, or gate
the anti-drift upgrade does not create a new lifecycle stage
